It will at best remain a niche target. So what could this launch actually be about? I think the answer is pretty simple - VR. If you've never tried it you'd think a company would insane to relaunch their hardware just to support it. If you have tried it, you'd think a company would be insane to not relaunch their hardware just to support it.

Consequently framing these relaunches as for 4k sounds nice and passively appealing whereas relaunching for VR would sound gimmicky and a turn-off for those who have yet to get to try it out. And the timing - these systems are coming at just about the point that we'd expect if they started R&Ding hard when more companies started realizing where VR was headed. Perhaps one thing I think we might expect to see, which would be a huge tell, is if one of the companies announces they're using a dual-GPU setup. That doesn't make all that much sense for traditional gaming and adds a good deal of complexity for developers, but it makes perfect sense when optimizing hardware for a VR focused setup. I don't think they'll go this route since they obviously want greater performance all around (and not just for VR) in which case one steak GPU is much better than a couple of pork chops, but if they do go that route it's a giant flashing VR VR VR billboard.

So to answer your question, no. If they do what I think they're doing - they're going to be able to put out some ground breaking quality VR in a package that's a fraction of what you'd pay to build and purchase yourself. It would really help distinguish consoles as a desirable gaming medium again.

A dual GPU setup in a piece of midrange hardware with months if not years of prior design makes no sense. The single GPU solution is cheaper, cooler and smaller for the same performance, even with great scaling.

You missed the biggest downside of all - developer support. The PS3 was a beast, in theory, but pretty mediocre in practice since the hardware was difficult to develop for. Multi-GPU architectures add substantial developmental difficulty. The returns are I think a bit more debatable. We haven't even scratched the surface of multi-GPU potential and comparing what we currently see on the consumer market to what's possible, particularly in a dedicated hardware/software setup isn't very telling of the potential of the hardware. The stereoscopic rendering of VR in particular really opens the door to some extreme optimization potential. But in any case I do agree that if they are not focusing on VR for this relaunch it would be extremely unlikely to see such hardware.

I also don't think we're going to see midrange hardware. Yet more predictions. I don't think the companies are going to make that mistake again.
